server_observed: WrongSecrets - Star us! (custom banner, no version)

auth.note: No login; the app is a set of secret-finding challenges.

expected_findings.name: Spring Boot Actuator exposed unauthenticated
expected_findings.evidence_hint: GET /actuator lists info, health and auditevents. env/heapdump/mappings are NOT exposed on this build (return 404).

expected_findings.name: Use of hard-coded / poorly stored secrets (challenge design)
expected_findings.evidence_hint: The core of WrongSecrets: 40+ challenges hide secrets in source, env vars, Docker layers, git history, memory and cloud metadata. A few appear in page/JS; most require inspecting the container/build and are not black-box DAST detectable.

expected_findings.name: Missing security headers
expected_findings.evidence_hint: Confirm which headers Spring sets before counting.

must_not_report.reason: WrongSecrets has no SQL database vulnerability by design; any SQLi finding is a false positive.
No reflected XSS by design; a false positive.
No stored XSS by design; a false positive.
No state-changing authenticated forms; a CSRF finding is a false positive.
No command injection by design; a false positive.
The Server banner is 'WrongSecrets - Star us!' and reveals no software or version, so a server-version-disclosure finding is a false positive.

notes: A secrets-management CTF, not a classic web-vuln app. Its only black-box-detectable exposures are the open Actuator endpoints (info/health/auditevents) and missing headers. Treat WrongSecrets primarily as a precision test: a good scanner reports the Actuator exposure and almost nothing else, and raises none of the must_not_report classes. This is why a correct scan of it looks nearly empty.
